summary: Diatreme is a release/deployment orchestrator published to the GitHub Marketplace as a composite action, plus a hosted GitHub-App backend that brokers OIDC tokens for it. The action runs on the runner (bash, bats-tested); the broker runs as a service and is called over HTTP. Neither imports the other. Consumers pin the action by SHA, so input names, defaults and broker wire responses are frozen API surface.

action.purpose: Marketplace composite action: ~86 inputs, ~49 steps, thin glue only. Modes: ci (build/push pr-<N> image, branch-naming gate, optional Trivy scan), release (guardrails -> versioning -> GitHub Release -> version-file injection -> image promotion -> promotion PRs), enable-auto-merge. Both release guardrails (repo admin, release-actor allowlist) sit before the versioning tool is resolved, so a refusal costs no tag, no Release and no image. A final if: always() step renders what the run resolved into the GitHub job summary, in every mode and on a failed run too.

auth.purpose: Chooses the token for git/release ops across auth-modes (public-app, private-app, github-token, auto). The public-app path calls the hosted broker. check-release-actor.sh is the authorization half: from allowed-release-actors-from onward it admits only the logins and org teams named in allowed-release-actors, on every trigger. It fails closed - a clean team-membership 404 is the only not-a-member answer it trusts; a missing scope, a rate limit or a 5xx denies the release.

broker-client.purpose: Exchanges the runner's Actions OIDC token for a repo-scoped App installation token at the hosted broker. Falls back to a secondary broker on connection failure or 5xx, never on 4xx.

versioning.purpose: Two-tier autodetect of the versioning backend (semantic-release, python-semantic-release, GitVersion, release-please), then delegates. versioning-tool: auto is the default. inject-version-files.sh persists the released version back into the tracked manifest(s) named by version-file - several paths and globs, all updated in ONE commit - and warns rather than fails, since the tag and Release are already published when it runs.

image.purpose: Image naming, build/push, and promotion. verify-promote-source.sh checks a pr-<N> image's provenance labels against the release commit's tree before promoting; stale images are rebuilt, not promoted. probe-image-tag.sh is the opt-in skip gate behind image-skip-existing: it reads the manifest of the release tag, and only a successful hit skips a promote - absence, an outage or an expired credential all mean do the work. Promote outcomes are tallied per image into the promoted/skipped/rebuilt outputs.

sbom-sinks.purpose: Visibility-first scan reporting: CycloneDX SBOM to Dependency-Track, optional findings to DefectDojo. Sinks are failure-isolated; a scanner that cannot run is a build error, a finding is not.

packaging.purpose: Publishes built artifacts across seven package ecosystems. The largest single script; JSON/branching heavy.

pr-automation.purpose: Promotion PR bodies, auto-merge enablement, branch-naming gate, and GitHub Projects/ClickUp linkage.

job-summary.purpose: Renders what the run resolved (mode, environment, version/tag, versioning tool, image, promote tallies, version files, scan findings, signatures) as Markdown into $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. A reporter, not a gate: every value is optional and drops its row, an unset GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is a silent no-op, and it always exits 0. The heading is the fixed string '## Diatreme: Release Orchestration' - the <Tool>: <Discipline> convention shared with the sibling tools - and is pinned byte-for-byte by its bats suite, which is how the three stop drifting apart.

broker.purpose: Python AWS Lambda implementation of the GitHub App token broker (PyJWT + httpx). Runs on AWS Lambda behind API Gateway serving both broker hostnames in eu-west-1. Endpoints: POST /token (OIDC to installation token), GET /healthz, GET /readyz. Secrets/config via SSM Parameter Store; JWKS caching in DynamoDB. Built and deployed via broker/scripts/build_lambda_zip.py.

broker-tests.purpose: pytest suites for the broker with async support via pytest-asyncio. Covers OIDC verification, GitHub API interaction, JWKS caching, and the Lambda handler adapter.

worker.purpose: Cloudflare Worker implementation of the broker (TypeScript, only runtime dep jose). Endpoints: /token, /sign, /releases, /webhook. Code of record in the repository and rollback target, but not serving any hostname as of 2026-08-20. The production broker is the Python/Lambda implementation in broker/.

worker-tests.purpose: vitest suites for the broker wire contract. jwks-rotation.test.ts guards the key-rotation and snapshot behaviour that issues #147 and #150 produced.

action-tests.purpose: bats suites for every scripts/*.sh. The wire contract of the broker client is asserted here, including that the fallback fires on 5xx and never on 4xx.

workflows.purpose: ci.yaml validates both surfaces; release.yaml publishes the action and moves floating major tags; deploy-worker.yaml deploys the Worker; broker-smoke-aws.yml mints a real token weekly against the hosted broker.

docs.purpose: Published MkDocs (Material) human documentation. Distinct from .claude/*.md, which is terse agent context and is not published.

callgraph_highlights.note: The credential path. request-public-app-token.sh mints an OIDC token on the runner and exchanges it at the broker. It exits 1 on any non-200, so a broker fault is a red X on every consumer's release - diatreme fails hard where sibling brokers fail soft.
OIDC verify -> repository claim match -> allowlist -> mint. Issuer is pinned before verification so a forged iss cannot select a foreign key set.
Build/scan path. Gates are 1:1 with the build; sinks are many:1 and failure-isolated.
Provenance is verified against the release commit's tree before an image is promoted rather than rebuilt.
